newsitem.title: USA: SEC charges another in APL case.
newsitem.headline: SEC charges another in APL case.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday it has added an additional defendant to its insider trading case involving APL Ltd securities.

In its civil case filed in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, the agency charged Lum Kwan Sung, a Singapore businessman, with insider trading in APL, an Oakland, Calif., provider of ocean-going cargo transportation services.
The SEC alleged that on February 25, Lum Kwan Sung opened a trading account and between February 25 and March 18 purchased 190,100 APL shares representing a $4.4 million investment.

The SEC alleged Lum Kwan Sung made an illegal profit after shares in APL rose on April 14 by $8.25 one day after the company announced it would be acquired by Singapore-based Neptune Orient Lines Ltd for $825 million.

"After the transaction was announced, the value of Lum's investment increased by over $1.2 million, a 27 percent return in just under seven weeks. The Commission alleges that Lum Kwan Sung made his purchases of APL stock while in possession of material, nonpublic information about the transaction," the SEC said in its complaint.

"Lum is a Singapore businessman who knows 'quite a few people' at the Singapore-based Neptune Orient, including two senior members of Neptune Orient's management who were intimately involved in the company's decision making and negotiations with respect to the acquisition," the agency wrote in its complaint.

In addition, the agency said Lum is the executive chairman of a company that owns a brokerage firm that is a member of the Singapore Stock Exchange, which was advised of the potential acquisition the day before Lum started buying APL stock. The complaint did not name the brokerage firm.
Lum Kwan Sung could not be reached for comment and SEC attorneys said he does not have an attorney representing him.
Charges were first filed by the SEC on April 15 against Ong Congqin Bobby, a Singapore man and, at the time, one other "unknown party."
According to press reports, Ong has said he did not act improperly and expects to be vindicated.

The agency, in its latest complaint filed Friday, also accused a London man, Abdul Ismail, of insider trading. Charges were filed against Ismail in the April 15 complaint, but the agency at that time was not able to identify him because he conducted his trades anonymously through a Swiss account, the SEC alleged.

The SEC alleges Ong Congqin Bobby and Abdul Ismail bought call options in APL on April 11, prior to the company's public announcement on April 13 that it would be acquired. The agency said both men's options trades represented 74 percent of APL option volume in certain series that day.
